# Step 0.10: Keep the page builder and the rich text editor off screens that do not edit a page

Phase 0 (Before the doors open) of `docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11.md`. Effort M. Read [how to carry out a step](../README.md) first.

**Who:** a smaller model; a stronger one reads the diff before the push. The work is file moves, import path changes and one lazy stand-in, proved by the build's figures, but it spans about 45 files, moves permission-guarded views and changes when a form's editor wakes up, so a stronger model should read the diff and the signed-in run.

**Goal:** No admin screen outside the page builder's own editors loads the rich text editor or the builder in its first scripts: previews, page lists, content lists, orders, customers, deals and the product editor load what they draw.

**Why:** Today 13 preview routes load the whole 3.3 MB builder (3,303,372 bytes), and 34 routes outside the builder load the rich text editor: an order page is 1,998,644 bytes and a product's editor 2,130,796. After: a preview at or under 1,450,000, an order page at or under 1,350,000, the product editor under 1,300,000, and 0 routes outside the builder's family with the editor.

**Closes:** [AC-2](../../findings/admin-browser/AC-2.md), [BN-14](../../findings/client-bundles/BN-14.md), [AC-3](../../findings/admin-browser/AC-3.md), [BN-5](../../findings/client-bundles/BN-5.md), [DP-5](../../findings/dependencies/DP-5.md). Each finding's file has the evidence.

## Do not

- Do not lazy-load the editor inside the page builder (page-builder.tsx line 96, block-fields.tsx line 33 keep their direct import): that is a later step.
- Do not use dynamic(..., { ssr: false }) for the field editor: a unit test holds that the server draws the field.
- Do not change what page-content.ts exports, and do not move any schema or block type out of it besides the rich text part.
- Do not leave a re-export of a moved view in editor-views.tsx or views.tsx: the import would bring the editor back.
- Do not do only the store's half: every move has a platform twin in the same commit.
- Do not change the words of the address-change sentence or of any catalogue.
- Do not raise a budget, and do not delete a permission guard entry: change the file it names.
- Do not split terms.tsx or move TermPicker (finding BN-5 step 6 is optional and not needed for the figures).

## Stop and report if

- The rich text lines of page-content.ts use zod or a page-model helper that cannot move with them.
- src/lib/custom-fields.ts or another file in the product editor's client closure still imports page-content after the edits: report the chain (the review's simulation expects the closure to fall from 157 files to 106).
- permissions.scan.test.ts fails for a reason other than the two guard entries.
- After the build the product editor is 1,300,000 bytes or more, or an order page above 1,350,000: report the ten largest first-load chunks of that route and what each holds; do not add more dynamic imports on your own.
- A unit test that draws a form shows the fallback box instead of the editor (the eager-lazy mock is not applied to that test's setup).
- The hand check loses typed text.

The step's 'product editor's English import sites' were not named anywhere, so I walked the product editor's client imports: two catalogues arrive through one helper each, redirects.en through addressChangeWords (src/lib/redirect-admin.ts) and fields.en through moveItem (src/lib/field-group-editor.ts), and the 197 KB page model through custom-fields.ts.
